text:
maria: Heads-up — we have a perf canary fail on the decode path after last night's merge (PR #4821). p95 up ~1.5x on short+long mixed workloads.
kevin: saw the alert. CI shows p95 jump from 48ms -> 72ms on rw-smallseq suite. throughput down ~18%. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/4821/canary
ash: repro locally with --profile-decode: token/sec drops 140k -> 115k on a 4xA100 job. attaching small flame summary: 
```
# flame top
decode_loop -> attn_kernel_dispatch -> attn_kv_batched_v2 (50%)
memcpy H2D (20%)
fallback_kernel (15%)
other (15%)
```
maria: interesting that attn_kv_batched_v2 shows up heavy; this merge touched the kernel selector and warmup prefetch logic.
nora: CI diff shows kernel router behavior changed: instead of steering short sequences to attn_scalar_fast, it sometimes routes to the batched path causing extra KV prefetch churn. commit abc1234 in PR 4821 is the culprit candidate.
perf-bot: perf-bot reports: p95_latency:+24ms (50 -> 74), throughput:-17.9%, memcpy_stalls:+12.3% (H2D), sm_util:+6% (but more idle gaps). See /perf/2026/2245607/report.html
kevin: ran a quick bisect. git bisect points to abc1234 as first bad commit. Reverting that commit locally restores baseline.
ash: I also profiled GPU timeline: the batched kernel issues extra small memcpy calls for prefix material due to new prefetch stride. That increases kernel launch overhead for short sequences. nsight snippet: 
```
Memcpy H2D 12 calls, mean 0.6ms
Kernel launches 24 extra calls per batch
```
maria: OK. Two potential immediate actions: 1) hold canary and disable new router flag (FEATURE_USE_NEW_ROUTER=false) on canary machines, 2) prepare a revert of abc1234 for rollout hold.
nora: +1 to holding canary. We should also test a targeted patch: tighten the warmup prefetch boundary so short sequences don't trigger the batched prefetch. Patch idea: if seq_len < 32 && batch_count < 8 -> use scalar path.
ben: I'm happy to take the revert PR if we want fast rollback. I can open revert/4821 in few minutes.
ci-bot: Notice: affected test suites: rw-smallseq, mixed-latency-load, prefix-cache-regression. Canary clusters: eu-west-1-prod-canary-2 flagged.
kevin: small experiment: toggling REWRITE_KERNEL_ROUTER=false on a single canary node brought p95 back to 49ms and token/sec to 138k within 10 minutes. That confirms routing is root cause (not fused op codegen).
maria: OK plan: Ben opens revert PR and we'll hold the rollout (block automatic promotion). Nora to prototype warmup-boundary patch and run microbenchmarks. Kevin to flip router flag on canaries now. Ash to prepare perf artifacts for post-mortem.
ben: opened revert PR #4850 -> revert commit abc1234. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/4850
ash: running microbench harness on patched warmup-boundary now, will post numbers in ~30m.
maria: thanks. Also file an incident ticket so support/ops are aware and we can coordinate customer-facing comms if needed.
kevin: added rollout-hold tag to release in the console and disabled router on canary nodes. metrics look good so far.
perf-bot: canary metrics after flag flip: p95_latency:49ms, throughput:+13% vs failing canary. Persisting for 22 minutes.
nora: updated design doc draft for safer prefetch: https://docs.internal/warmup-prefetch-design (notes on heuristics and metrics to watch).
maria: closing the thread for now — we'll reconvene after revert merges or warmup patch lands. Great triage everyone. :thumbsup:
